solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 'Ask me out to party', so gets along

indicators.note: out suggests the words are put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone invites a person out to a party and so they get along together.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with what is available, which is to get by or get along.

clue.text: Reckless general's assistant involved in plan

indicators.note: involved in places one piece inside the other, wrapped up within the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart of an area
ADC stands for aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a general

explanation.surface: A rash aide to a general gets caught up in a military plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap person acts wildly and impulsively, a close synonym for rash or reckless behaviour.

clue.text: Take ground with artilleryman entering unarmed combat

indicators.note: entering puts the gunner's letters inside the rearranged word
ground as a past participle means crushed or worked over, so the word Take is rearranged

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner in crosswords

explanation.surface: An order to seize territory while a gunner joins in a fight without weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take ground' reads as seizing territory, but 'ground' is the anagram signal working on Take; RA, the Royal Artillery, is a crossword gunner.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of striking with hands and feet, a form of fighting without weapons.

clue.text: Its constructors must meet high conditions

definitions.text: Its constructors must meet high conditions

parts.words: Its constructors must meet high conditions
parts.note: high conditions sounds like demanding standards but literally means working at great height, as builders of very tall towers do

explanation.surface: Builders of some project are held to exacting standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers building the tallest city towers literally labour in lofty conditions far above street level.

clue.text: Samuel's teacher is after old boy with daggers drawn

indicators.note: is after places the teacher's name following the old boy's letters

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
Eli was the priest who raised and taught the prophet Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A prophet's old tutor follows a former pupil, at daggers drawn with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With daggers drawn' reads as hostility, but the daggers are printed marks, drawn with a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger-shaped printer's mark used for footnotes, so the plural names several such drawn marks.

clue.text: Flashing lights bringing movement to a stop?

definitions.text: Flashing lights bringing movement to a stop?

parts.words: Flashing lights bringing movement to a stop?
parts.note: rapidly pulsing lamps make moving dancers appear frozen in a series of still images

explanation.surface: Perhaps emergency lights halting traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroboscopic lamps flash fast enough that moving things seem to stand still between flashes.

clue.text: One with a political belief that's not right

definitions.text: One with a political belief that's not right

parts.words: One with a political belief that's not right
parts.note: not right reads as wrong, but means on the left of politics

explanation.surface: Someone holding a mistaken political view.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in collective ownership sits on the political left, the side opposite the right.

clue.text: One may call it a breakfast stand-by

definitions.meaning: a register of names read aloud is a ... call
a bread bun is a dependable morning staple

explanation.definitionFit: A roll is both the list of names called out and a small bread loaf eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Barely used part of the house

definitions.text: Barely used part of the house

parts.words: Barely used part of the house
parts.note: barely seems to mean hardly ever but means used while bare, without clothes

explanation.surface: A spare room in a home that hardly anyone goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: The room for washing is where people are routinely naked, so it is used by the bare.

clue.text: Had a fight, getting thrown out

definitions.meaning: to scrap is to brawl or quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: Scrapping is slang for fighting, and something scrapped has been discarded as junk.

clue.text: A classic hat worn by Americans

definitions.meaning: the Epsom race of that name is one of the five English Classic horse races
the US word for a bowler hat

explanation.walkthrough: The Classics are five major British flat horse races; this one is run at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a famous Epsom horse race, a Classic, and the American name for a bowler hat.

clue.text: Non-stop passenger-carrying flight

parts.note: flight reads as an aeroplane journey but is a flight of stairs that keeps moving

explanation.surface: A direct airline service carrying travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase is a flight of steps that carries people continuously without stopping.

clue.text: Claim tax in crooked endeavour that ends in disappointment

indicators.note: crooked means bent or twisted out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A dishonest scheme to claim tax back fails to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort that builds up and then fizzles out is a letdown, a disappointing finish.

clue.text: Luggage in hold?

definitions.meaning: an old word for a travelling bag
a firm clasp or grasp of something in the hand

explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a holdall or travel bag, and also a firm clasp on something.

clue.text: Crashing gears gives feeling full of hostility

indicators.note: crashing gears grind badly, signalling these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver crunching the gearbox is left in a combative mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hostile and confrontational in attitude is the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Local place for refreshing game

definitions.meaning: a local is a British term for one's nearby pub
a pool where wild animals come to drink

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub; 'game' here is wild animals, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a pub, jokingly, and a pool where wild animals gather to drink.

clue.text: Wrapped up in unusually deep novel

indicators.note: unusually suggests an odd arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in a strange, profound book.
explanation.definitionFit: To be covered completely, encased or wrapped, is the meaning of this past participle.

clue.text: Filmed under cover

definitions.meaning: shown on a cinema or TV screen
... also means hidden or sheltered behind a partition

explanation.definitionFit: Screened means shown on film or television, and also concealed behind a screen.

clue.text: Trouble international group has to resolve

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, a body of many nations
to settle a matter is to resolve it

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out that the United Nations must sort out.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or upset someone's calm is to trouble them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Unusual controversy about a school of music

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter
unusual suggests the letters appear in an unexpected order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd row breaks out around a music academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatoire, or in this spelling the related word, is a college for training musicians.

clue.text: Feast set out around Italian capital for religious celebration

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on either side of the single letter
set out suggests laying things out afresh, so the letters are rearranged
capital means the head or first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A feast laid out around an Italian city to mark a holy day.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish saint's day festival is a religious holiday with feasting and processions.

clue.text: Fly spitfire by day

parts.note: a spitfire is a fiery, bad-tempered woman, a shrew

explanation.surface: Flying the wartime fighter plane by daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly in British slang means sharp-witted and knowing, the same as astute.

clue.text: Observers usually working in pairs

parts.note: observers sounds like watchers or police but means the organs of sight, which come two at a time

explanation.surface: Lookouts who normally operate two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight see things and almost always come as a matched pair.

clue.text: Worker who is constantly striking

parts.note: striking reads as an industrial walkout but means hammering hot iron at an anvil

explanation.surface: A trade unionist who is always out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith forging iron hammers metal on an anvil all day long.

clue.text: Fifty or a hundred will come up to sing

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Fifty or a hundred singers will turn up for a choral performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will come up' turns LORAC upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing joyfully, especially festive songs.

clue.text: Pass taken out for health resorts

indicators.note: taken out suggests the letters are pulled out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A travel pass used on trips to spa towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Towns with mineral springs where people go for treatment are the resorts named here.

clue.text: School rejected exam questions and corresponding material

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
an exam paper is the set of questions in a test

explanation.surface: A pupil turned away from a top school is left with only test questions.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets used for writing letters are stationery for correspondence.

clue.text: Children may be a contentious point

explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring in legal language, and also a subject under debate.

clue.text: Lined up in uniform?

definitions.meaning: in drill, troops dress ranks by aligning themselves

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers dress their ranks by forming a straight line, and dressed also means clothed.

clue.text: General protection away from the wind

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
ward means guard or protection, as in ward off

explanation.surface: A commander offers shelter on the downwind side.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side facing away from the wind is the nautical sense here.
